description: Full dump of every entity on the current lot with exact tile coordinates. Unlike query-nearby (range-limited around the bot's position), this enumerates the entire VM entity list. Use this to plan placements: read the existing layout, pick an empty tile, then issue buy-object. Skips multi-tile non-root entries so a 2x3 object returns one entry per multitile-group, not six. Optional level filter narrows to one floor; optional guid_hex filter narrows to one catalog class. Pure local-VM read — no PDU, no transaction. Companion to the host-side fsov-dump tool which reads the same data from saved .fsov state files; this convention reads the live VM and stays current between SaveRing ticks.

args.name: level
args.description: Filter to a single floor (0..3). Omit for all floors.

args.name: guid_hex
args.description: Filter to a single catalog class GUID, e.g. "0x675C18AF" (Fridge - Cheap). Cross-reference GameAssets/TSOClient/packingslips/catalog.xml. Omit for all classes.

call_signatures: cf $CF query-lot-objects --guid_hex 0x675C18AF                                        # only Fridge - Cheap entities
common_mistakes: Treating x/y as subtiles. They are tile coords (already divided by 16). Multiply by 16 when passing to buy-object's x/y subtile args.
Using object_id when send-to-inventory needs persist_id. delete-object uses object_id; send-to-inventory uses persist_id.
Forgetting that the bot must be on the same lot. query-lot-objects always reflects the lot the bot is currently joined to.
perception_hints: Compare against perception.nearby_objects[] to confirm a placement landed within the bot's view radius.
guid_hex matches the catalog GUID for the object class. The catalog name (e.g. 'Fridge - Cheap') comes from packingslips/catalog.xml.
Empty tile detection: for each candidate (x,y,level), iterate the response and check no entry has matching tile coords.
refuse_conditions: no live VM (bot not joined to a lot yet) → ok:false 'no live VM'
